Trial For McCormick and McWilliams Set For November 16;
Ruling on Defense Motions Expected On October 12.
"Who will speak for the United States?"

Special to MarijuanaNews
August 9, 1999
Los Angeles, CA

By Richard Cowan

Today, Federal Judge George King set a November 16 date for the long expected trial of medical marijuana activists Todd McCormick and Peter McWilliams.

See
September 7th Trial Date Set For McCormick and McWilliams;

He also said that he will rule on the numerous defense motions – including a motion to suppress all the evidence taken in the raid on McCormick’s home-- on Columbus Day. A favorable ruling on some of the key motions would eliminate the necessity for a trial. Perhaps he will rediscover America.

Judge King appears to be exceptionally intelligent, but there is no way to anticipate how he will rule. Originally, the government had said that the trial could take up to eight weeks, which would have delayed the trial until after the first of the year; however, the judge made very clear that he did not expect it to last more than two weeks, and he did not want it to be drawn out any further and set the November date.

One of the most important defense motions deals with the issue of "selective prosecution" and raises important First Amendment questions. Why is the government prosecuting two outspoken advocates while allowing prosecution witnesses to continue to buy, sell and grow medical marijuana?
See
Was The Decision To Prosecute B. E. Smith Made At The White House?
The Key Question About The Selective Prosecution Of Medical Marijuana Activists.
Analysis -- By Richard Cowan

As well-know author and AIDS patient Peter McWilliams sat in a wheelchair with his head down, the lawyers wrestled with procedural questions, all based on the premise that the government is dangerous to our liberties.

It must be exceptionally nightmarish for McWilliams who has made a career of warning about the threat to freedom posed by the overarching power of this government to find that they are willing to kill him and others in order to suppress medical marijuana. Of course, that is what is really going on behind all of the pomp and circumstance.

I found it truly surreal watching the proceedings. At the end of the defense’s presentation of its motions the judge asked the standard question: "Who will speak for the United States?"

Of course, I knew what he meant, but it still brought to mind the lyrics from the great Steppenwolf song, Monster - Suicide – America:
"America where are you now?
Don’t you care about your sons and daughters?
Don’t you know we need you now?
We can’t fight alone against the monster."

Where indeed?
"Who will speak for the United States?"
